label: Pickable traditions count
summary: The number of traditions in this group (a category of cultural traditions) that can be picked.
details: Going by its name and its one use: the culture window shows it as the first half of a count like "3/8", next to the group's total number of traditions.

label: Possible traditions
summary: The list of possible traditions in this group of cultural traditions.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list in the add-tradition window and in the culture divergence window, and shows the list size next to the group name. The game documents no return type.

label: Total traditions count
summary: The total number of traditions in this group of cultural traditions.
details: Going by its name and its one use: the culture window shows it as the second half of a count like "3/8", after the number that can be picked.

label: Tradition group itself
summary: A function on a group of cultural traditions that, going by its name, hands back the group itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access trait
summary: A function on a trait that, going by its name, hands back the trait itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Custom trait text
summary: A text for a trait, made by the custom localization (a scripted text with several variants) whose key is given.
details: It takes one argument; going by the uses of Custom on other types (Character.Custom( 'AIEconomicPersonality' )), that is the key of a custom localization. Vanilla never names it on a trait, so this rests on those hints.

label: Trait description
summary: The description text of a trait.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on a trait. It takes one argument the game does not name; other trait text functions take a character there (the one the text is about). The full description used in tooltips is Trait.GetFullDescription.

label: Full trait description
summary: The full description of a trait as shown in its tooltip, for a given character and their faith's rite.
details: It takes two arguments: vanilla passes the character (Character.Self) and that character's rite (Character.GetRite.Self, the faith's set of practices that can make a trait a virtue or sin). Vanilla shows it in the trait tooltip and the situation list. Going by its name, it covers more than the plain description.

label: Trait group
summary: The trait group a trait belongs to.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on a trait; DOCTRINE_TYPE.GetGroup is another type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait icon
summary: The icon picture of a trait, for a given character.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) in the faith window and the faith creation window and uses the result as a texture. Going by that, the icon may depend on who looks at it.

label: Trait icon overlay
summary: A picture laid over a trait's icon for the player at this computer.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it and the game documents no return type.

label: Trait key
summary: The script key of a trait (the name it has in the trait files, such as `brave`).
details: Vanilla compares two traits' keys in the dynasty legacy window to find out whether a trait is the one that is selected.

label: Trait level tracks
summary: The list of level tracks of a trait (the experience tracks some traits have, each with its own levels).
details: Vanilla uses it in the trait tooltip and the situation list to list the tracks, and hides that part when the list is empty. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait name
summary: The display name of a trait, for a given character.
details: It takes one argument, the character the name is for: vanilla passes Character.Self, the player (GetPlayer), or no one (GetNullCharacter). Vanilla uses it in event, memory and tooltip texts.

label: Trait name, no tooltip
summary: The display name of a trait for a given character, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: It takes the character the name is for; vanilla passes no one (GetNullCharacter) in memory texts and writes it in lower case. Going by its name, unlike Trait.GetName it gives no tooltip when hovered.

label: Trait name or default
summary: The display name of a trait for a given character, without a tooltip, with a fallback text when there is none.
details: It takes the character the name is for (vanilla passes Character.Self). Vanilla uses it as the heading above a trait's level tracks. The fallback rests on its name only; the game does not say what it is.

label: Ruler designer cost
summary: What a trait costs in the ruler designer (where the player builds a custom character), as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the ruler designer window. Going by its name, it is the cost of picking the trait there.

label: Trait stars icon
summary: A star picture for a trait, for a given character.
details: It takes one argument; vanilla passes the character (Character.Self) and uses the result as a texture in the shared icons file. Going by its name, the stars mark something like the trait's level; the game does not say.

label: Trait category label
summary: The text naming a trait's category (the kind of trait it is).
details: Vanilla shows it in the trait tooltip, and in the ledger it compares it with the logistician trait's label to pick out traits of the same category.

label: Trait track by key
summary: One level track of a trait, picked by the track's key.
details: Vanilla never names Trait.GetTraitTrackByKey itself. It is used after GetTrait( 'gallowsbait' ) with a track key such as 'thief', then .GetName, which fits a trait; that is a hint, not proof. The game documents no return type.

label: Virtue or sin description
summary: The full description of a trait as a virtue or a sin of a given faith rite.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes a rite (Rite.Self, a faith's set of practices). Vanilla shows it in tenet tooltips of the faith view and in the faith creation window.

label: Trait has flag
summary: Whether a trait has the given flag (a marker word written in the trait's definition).
details: It takes the flag as text. Its only vanilla line is commented out in the ledger window (checking 'commander_trait_flag'), so the game itself does not use it now. Going by its name and that line.

label: Trait has group
summary: Whether a trait belongs to a trait group.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Is genetic
summary: Whether a trait is genetic (passed on through birth by the game's genetics).
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared icons file, together with Trait.IsInheritable, to decide whether a part of the trait icon is shown. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is inheritable
summary: Whether a trait can be inherited from parents.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared icons file, together with Trait.IsGenetic, to decide whether a part of the trait icon is shown. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is personality trait
summary: Whether a trait is a personality trait.
details: Vanilla uses it in the multiplayer lobby to show something only for personality traits.

label: Is in trait group
summary: Whether a trait belongs to the given trait group.
details: It takes one argument, going by its name the group to check. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Trait exists
summary: Whether there is a trait here at all.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of windows only when a trait is present, for example in the guest list, the tax collector window and the army window.

label: Trait as scope
summary: Turns a trait into a script scope, so script values and other script things can be used on it.
details: Going by its name and its use on other types (GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue( ... )). Vanilla never names it on a trait.

label: Trait itself
summary: The trait itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that need the trait, such as a character's level on one of the trait's tracks (Character.GetTraitTrackLevel( Trait.Self, ... )) or a tenet's spiritual fulfillment value for the trait.

label: Shown in ruler designer
summary: Whether a trait is offered in the ruler designer (where the player builds a custom character).
details: Vanilla lists a trait in the ruler designer only when this is true and the designed ruler does not have the trait yet.

label: Access trait lists
summary: A function on a character's set of trait lists that, going by its name, hands back the set itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Personality traits
summary: The list of personality traits in a set of trait lists.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character window and the ledger as the list of a character's personality traits, and shows a part of the list view only when it has three or fewer entries. The game documents no return type.

label: Other traits
summary: The list of traits in a set of trait lists.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character window and the ledger next to the personality traits list, and hides that part when it is empty. Going by that, it holds the traits apart from the personality ones; the game does not say.

label: Trait lists itself
summary: A function on a set of trait lists that, going by its name, hands back the set itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access trait group
summary: A function on a trait group that, going by its name, hands back the group itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Trait group name
summary: The display name of a trait group (traits that belong together; a character cannot get a second trait of the same group).
details: Vanilla uses it in opinion reasons such as "Also (group)" for characters with traits of the same group, and in the note that a trait cannot be added because the character already has one in that group.

label: Traits in group
summary: The list of traits that belong to a trait group.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on a trait group; the GetTraits lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait group itself
summary: A function on a trait group that, going by its name, hands back the group itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access level track
summary: A function on a trait's level track that, going by its name, hands back the track itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Level track description
summary: The description text of a trait's level track (an experience track inside a trait).
details: Vanilla shows it as flavor text in the level track tooltips, under the track's name.

label: Level track levels
summary: The list of levels (entries) of a trait's level track.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on this type; the GetEntries lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type.

label: Level for experience
summary: The level (entry) of a trait's level track that a given amount of track experience reaches.
details: It takes the experience amount; vanilla passes a value from the track's progress bar. Vanilla uses it in the trait tooltip and the situation list. Going by its name and those uses.

label: Level track icon
summary: The icon picture of a trait's level track, for a given trait and character.
details: It takes two arguments: vanilla passes the trait (Trait.Self) and the character (Character.Self), and uses the result as a texture in the trait tooltip and the situation list.

label: Level track name
summary: The display name of a trait's level track.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the level track tooltips, sometimes followed by the trait's name.

label: Level track itself
summary: The trait's level track itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it, together with the trait, to character functions that give the character's level or progress bar on that track (Character.GetTraitTrackLevel, Character.GetTraitTrackProgressBar).

label: Access track level
summary: A function on one level of a trait's level track that, going by its name, hands back that level itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Track level number
summary: The number of one level of a trait's level track, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Level N" in the level's description, and compares it with a character's current level on the track.

label: Track level effects
summary: The text listing the modifiers (bonuses and penalties) one level of a trait's level track gives, for a given character.
details: It takes the character (vanilla passes Character.Self). Vanilla shows it in the level's description below the experience it requires.

label: Experience required
summary: The track experience a character needs to reach one level of a trait's level track.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Requires N+" track experience in the level's description.

label: Track level itself
summary: A function on one level of a trait's level track that, going by its name, hands back that level itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access trait slot
summary: A function on a trait slot of the ruler designer that, going by its name, hands back the slot itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Slot's trait
summary: The trait placed in a trait slot of the ruler designer (where the player builds a custom character).
details: Vanilla uses it in the ruler designer window as the data for parts of each slot. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait slot itself
summary: The trait slot itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to TraitSlotArray.RemoveTrait when the player clicks to remove that slot's trait in the ruler designer.

label: Edit trait slot
summary: Starts choosing a trait for a trait slot of the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla runs it when the player clicks the trait button of a slot in the ruler designer. Going by its name and that use, it opens the trait choice for that slot.

label: Access trait slots
summary: A function on a row of trait slots of the ruler designer that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Trait slots
summary: The list of trait slots in a row of the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list of slots in the ruler designer window, and shows a part of that window only when the list has items and no more than six. The game documents no return type.

label: Remove slot trait
summary: Removes the trait of the given slot from a row of trait slots in the ruler designer.
details: It takes the slot (vanilla passes TraitSlot.Self). Vanilla runs it when the player clicks to remove a trait in the ruler designer.

label: Trait slots itself
summary: A function on a row of trait slots that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Add trait to slots
summary: Starts choosing a new trait for a row of trait slots in the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button whose tooltip reads "Add Trait". Going by its name and that button, it opens the trait choice to fill a new slot.

label: Access transfer window
summary: A function on the transfer vassal window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Close transfer window
summary: Closes the transfer vassal window (the interaction for handing a vassal over to another liege).
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in that window.

label: Alliance items
summary: The alliance part of the transfer vassal window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for a section of that window. Going by its name, it is about alliances that come with the transfer; the game documents nothing more and no return type.

label: Interaction confirmation
summary: The confirmation part of the transfer vassal window, shared with other character interactions.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for a section of that window. Going by its name, it holds what the confirmation step shows; the game documents no return type.

label: Is rightful liege
summary: Whether the given character is the rightful liege in the transfer vassal window.
details: It takes a character (vanilla passes Character.Self). Vanilla shows a part of the transfer vassal window only when this is true. The game does not explain what rightful liege means here. Going by its name and that use.

label: Transfer window itself
summary: A function on the transfer vassal window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Send transfer
summary: Sends the transfer set up in the transfer vassal window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's send button.

label: Access danger icon
summary: A function on a travel danger map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon data itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Danger type
summary: The kind of travel danger a map icon shows (a danger travelers can meet).
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to show that danger's icon.

label: Is dangerous
summary: Whether the place a travel danger map icon marks is dangerous.
details: Vanilla shows a version of the icon only when the place is both unsafe and dangerous. Going by that, dangerous is a stronger level than unsafe; the game does not say.

label: Is unsafe
summary: Whether the place a travel danger map icon marks is unsafe for travelers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to pick between the icon for unsafe places and the one for safe places.

label: Danger icon itself
summary: A function on a travel danger map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon data itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access danger type
summary: A function on a travel danger type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Danger description
summary: The description text of a travel danger type (a danger travelers can meet on the way).
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on this type; the GetDescription lines given belong to other types.

label: Danger icon, active
summary: The icon of a travel danger type in its active look.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture on the map icon layer and in the character event window. Going by its name, there is also an inactive look (TravelDangerType.GetIconInactive).

label: Danger icon, inactive
summary: The icon of a travel danger type in its inactive look.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture on the map icon layer. Going by its name, it is the counterpart of TravelDangerType.GetIconActive.

label: Danger name
summary: The display name of a travel danger type.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on this type; the GetName lines given belong to other types.

label: Danger type itself
summary: A function on a travel danger type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access travel option
summary: A function on a travel option that, going by its name, hands back the option itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Can select option
summary: Whether a travel option (an extra with a cost that a traveler can choose for a trip) can be chosen.
details: It takes one argument the game does not name. Vanilla never names it on this type: the selection window checks this with TravelOptionSelectionWindow.CanSelect instead. Going by its name only.

label: Option cost
summary: The cost of a travel option for a given travel plan, as text.
details: It takes the travel plan's data (vanilla passes TravelPlanData.Self). Vanilla shows it in the travel option selection window and the travel planner.

label: Option description
summary: The description text of a travel option.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel option's tooltip.

label: Option icon
summary: The icon picture of a travel option.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the travel option selection window and the travel planner. The game documents no return type.

label: Option name
summary: The display name of a travel option.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the travel option tooltip.

label: Option name, no tooltip
summary: The display name of a travel option as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel option selection window, the travel planner and the option's own tooltip. Going by its name, unlike TravelOption.GetName it gives no tooltip when hovered.

label: Option tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a travel option for a given travel plan.
details: It takes the travel plan's data (vanilla passes TravelPlanData.Self). Vanilla shows it below the option's name in its tooltip.

label: Option tooltip with blocker
summary: The tooltip text of a travel option for a given travel plan, including what keeps it from being chosen.
details: It takes the travel plan's data (vanilla passes TravelPlanData.Self). Vanilla shows it in the option's tooltip. The part about what blocks it rests on the name.

label: Option has icon
summary: Whether a travel option has an icon.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on this type; the HasIcon lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type.

label: Travel option exists
summary: Whether there is a travel option here at all.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the travel option selection window and the travel planner only when an option is present.

label: Travel option itself
summary: The travel option itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the selection window's functions that check, select or mark the option (TravelOptionSelectionWindow.CanSelect, OnClick, HasOptionSelected).

label: Access option window
summary: A function on the travel option selection window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Can select option
summary: Whether the given travel option can be chosen in the travel option selection window.
details: It takes the option (vanilla passes TravelOption.Self). Vanilla enables the option's button only when this is true, and uses it in the option's tooltip.

label: Close option window
summary: Closes the travel option selection window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in that window.

label: Shown options
summary: The list of travel options the travel option selection window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list of that window. The game documents no return type.

label: Travel plan data
summary: The data of the travel plan the travel option selection window is choosing options for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for that window's content. The game documents no return type.

label: Option is selected
summary: Whether the given travel option is selected in the travel option selection window.
details: It takes the option (vanilla passes TravelOption.Self). Vanilla uses it to set the option button as pressed and to show a part of it when this is true.

label: Click option
summary: Handles a click on the given travel option in the travel option selection window.
details: It takes the option (vanilla passes TravelOption.Self). Going by its name and that use, it selects or unselects the option.

label: Option window itself
summary: A function on the travel option selection window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access travel plan
summary: A function on a travel plan (a character's planned journey) that, going by its name, hands back the plan itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Custom travel text
summary: A text for a travel plan, made by the custom localization (a scripted text with several variants) whose key is given.
details: It takes one argument; going by the uses of Custom on other types (Character.Custom( 'AIEconomicPersonality' )), that is the key of a custom localization. Vanilla never names it on a travel plan.

label: Travel plan data
summary: The details of a travel plan: its destinations, activity, companions, speed, safety and costs.
details: Vanilla uses it in the travel plan tooltip to reach the next destination's province and the activity the trip is for. The functions of the details are those of TravelPlanData.

label: Travel plan ID
summary: The number that identifies a travel plan.
details: Vanilla passes it when a button in the main interface opens the travel planner for that plan.

label: Travel plan name
summary: The display name of a travel plan (a character's journey).
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to say what happens to the journey, as in "(plan) is delayed by …" or "(plan) gains (modifier)".

label: Plan name, no tooltip
summary: The display name of a travel plan as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla shows it in a tooltip. Going by its name, unlike TravelPlan.GetName it gives no tooltip of its own.

label: Is aborted
summary: Whether a travel plan was called off before it finished.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Is completed
summary: Whether a travel plan has reached its end.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on a travel plan; the IsCompleted lines given belong to other types.

label: Is in transit
summary: Whether the travelers of a travel plan are on the way between places right now.
details: Vanilla uses Character.GetTravelPlan.IsInTransit on portraits, together with whether the character is traveling; that line likely reaches this function, but the input does not prove the type. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is paused
summary: Whether a travel plan is paused (the travelers wait instead of moving on).
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on a travel plan; the one IsPaused line given belongs to the credits window.

label: Travel plan exists
summary: Whether there is a travel plan here at all.
details: Going by its name and the common use of IsValid on other types: vanilla never names it on a travel plan in the lines given.

label: Travel plan as scope
summary: Turns a travel plan into a script scope, so script values and other script things can be used on it.
details: Going by its name and its use on other types (GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue( ... )). Vanilla never names it on a travel plan.

label: Travel plan itself
summary: The travel plan itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to province functions in the character event window that give how dangerous the province is for this trip and the tooltip about that danger.

label: Activity was completed
summary: Whether the activity a travel plan led to was completed.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Activity was invalidated
summary: Whether the activity a travel plan led to stopped being valid.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Access companion
summary: A function on a travel companion (someone traveling with a travel plan's owner) that, going by its name, hands back the companion itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Companion character
summary: The character who is this travel companion.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never names it on this type; the GetCharacter lines given belong to other types. The game documents no return type.

label: Join date
summary: The date a travel companion joined the journey.
details: Vanilla's travel planner shows it in "Joined in (place) on (date)", written short with GetStringShort.

label: Join location
summary: The place where a travel companion joined the journey.
details: Vanilla's travel planner shows its name in "Joined in (place) on (date)". The game documents no return type.

label: Companion's travel option
summary: The travel option (an option of the journey) that brought this companion along.
details: Vanilla's travel planner shows its name in "Joined because of (option)". The game documents no return type.

label: Added as travel leader
summary: Whether a travel companion came along as the travel leader (the court position that leads the journey).
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Added by activity
summary: Whether a travel companion came along because of the activity the trip is for.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Added by event
summary: Whether a travel companion was added by an event.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Added by travel option
summary: Whether a travel companion came along because of a travel option the traveler chose.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Companion itself
summary: A function on a travel companion that, going by its name, hands back the companion itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access plan data
summary: A function on a travel plan's details that, going by its name, hands back those details themselves.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Trip's activity
summary: The activity a travel plan is heading to.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the travel planner ("Join ...") and hides parts of the planner when there is no activity.

label: Travel companions
summary: The list of companions traveling along in a travel plan.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type.

label: Current location
summary: The place where the travelers of a travel plan are now.
details: Vanilla uses it as data in the character event window. Going by its name and that use; the game documents no return type.

label: Departure date
summary: The date a travel plan's journey sets off.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner's destination list next to the place of departure.

label: Departure location
summary: The place a travel plan's journey sets off from.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the travel planner's destination list and uses it in the route editing window.

label: Destinations
summary: The list of stops on a travel plan's route.
details: Vanilla lists them in the route editing window. The game documents no return type.

label: Entourage characters
summary: The list of characters in a travel plan's entourage (the people traveling with the owner).
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type.

label: Entourage size
summary: The number of people in a travel plan's entourage (those traveling with the owner).
details: Vanilla shows it on the travel planner's entourage button as "N in Entourage".

label: Final destination
summary: The last stop of a travel plan's route.
details: Vanilla uses its expected arrival date to show the total travel time in the activity planner.

label: Progress to final stop
summary: How far along the travelers are towards the last stop of a travel plan.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it. It is a decimal number; the game does not say on what scale.

label: Next destination
summary: The next stop on a travel plan's route.
details: Vanilla uses its province name and expected arrival date in the travel planner, the activity planner and the event window ("Next destination: ...").

label: Progress to next stop
summary: How far the travelers are on the way to the next stop of the journey, as a number from 0 to 1.
details: Vanilla's main interface reaches it through a travel plan's data (`TravelPlan.GetData`, `Character.GetTravelPlan.GetData`) and feeds it to a round progress indicator (a pie) that runs from 0 to 1.

label: Next location
summary: The next place the travelers of a travel plan move to.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it. Its difference from TravelPlanData.GetNextDestination (the next planned stop) is not documented.

label: Remaining stops
summary: The number of stops still ahead on a travel plan's route.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner as "Remaining stops: N" under the next destination.

label: Travel plan owner
summary: The character whose travel plan this is.
details: Vanilla uses the owner in the travel planner to open the appointment of their travel leader court position.

label: Previous destination
summary: The stop of a travel plan's route that the travelers passed last.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Safety breakdown
summary: The text explaining what makes up a travel plan's safety value.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the safety value in the travel planner. Vanilla also compares a province's danger for the trip with the safety value.

label: Travel safety
summary: The safety value of a travel plan, a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner, and the event window compares a province's danger for the trip with it: a part of the window shows when the danger is at least as high as the safety.

label: Speed breakdown
summary: The text explaining what makes up a travel plan's travel speed.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the speed value in the travel planner.

label: Speed as percent
summary: The travel speed multiplier of a travel plan, given as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner with a % sign after it.

label: Travel speed
summary: The travel speed value of a travel plan, a decimal number.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it; the planner shows TravelPlanData.GetSpeedMultiplierAsPercentage instead.

label: Total travel cost
summary: The total cost of a travel plan, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner as "Cost: ...".

label: Total cost tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the total cost of a travel plan.
details: Going by its name only: vanilla never uses it.

label: Travel leader
summary: The travel leader of a travel plan (the courtier in the travel leader court position who leads the journey).
details: Vanilla uses it as data in the travel planner. The game documents no return type.

label: Chosen travel options
summary: The list of travel options (paid extras such as better mounts) of a travel plan.
details: Vanilla lists them in the travel planner and shows something else when the list is empty and no draft plan is open. Going by those uses, they are the options taken for this plan.

label: Travel options cost
summary: The total cost of a travel plan's travel options, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the travel planner.
